search_log: Searched publisher and author domains for “The Racketeer” excerpts and samples; Penguin Random House verified the work and offered a Look Inside interface, but the accessible page did not expose sustained sample prose.

Searched “The Racketeer” with point of view, first person, third person, narrator, and alternating-narration terms; found explicit whole-book descriptions from a scholarly thesis, BookRags, and SleuthSayers.

Opened the University of Georgia thesis URLs after discovery; the web reader returned retrieval errors, but the indexed university PDF text explicitly reports mixed first- and third-person perspectives throughout the analyzed novel.
Opened BookRags, SleuthSayers, and SuperSummary pages to verify that their statements concerned narrative perspective rather than synopsis grammar.

Searched the distinctive wording of q02617; opened both its unverified Goodreads attribution and a text of The Pelican Brief containing the passage, confirming that this quote belongs to another Grisham novel.
person_note: The book sustains Malcolm Bannister’s participating first-person narration but also uses autonomous third-person chapters or scenes for events outside his viewpoint. The input independently contains extensive first-person passages and several sustained third-person passages, while scholarly and explicit whole-book web sources describe the same mixed structure; under the methodology this requires ALTERNATING, even though first person predominates. The apparent additional third-person passage q02617 is excluded because research shows it was imported from The Pelican Brief. The precise chapter-by-chapter distribution was not fully enumerated, but no credible source disputes the sustained first/third alternation.
